purpose: Resolve which source governs which kind of claim without flattening vision, build, product, evidence, repository state, and runtime proof into one authority level.

nodes.name: Explicit Current User Directive
nodes.description: Controls the current task's scope and requested mutation. Does not silently rewrite persistent project canon unless the directive explicitly changes the governing source.

nodes.name: DOC-A Vision Canon
nodes.description: Future/product vision. Not current build obligation by itself.

nodes.name: DOC-B System Law
nodes.description: Governs system identity, authority, output/freeze/imperfection laws.

nodes.name: DOC-C Build Spec
nodes.description: Exclusive source of current vNEXT build obligation unless explicitly extended/versioned.

nodes.name: DOC-D Product Design Pack
nodes.description: Concrete product/UI/storage/auth design subordinate to System Law and current Build Spec.

nodes.name: DOC-E Deployment Evidence Pack
nodes.description: Defines required proof for deployment approval; does not make implementation claims true merely by being specified.

nodes.name: Constitutional / Sovereign Locked Source
nodes.description: Governs future Sovereign/Universe/constitutional fabric within its declared scope; not automatically a DOC-C obligation.

nodes.name: Game Fabric Source
nodes.description: Governs deterministic AAAA/Game Fabric domain within future architecture scope.

nodes.name: Capability Governance Source
nodes.description: Governs NCF capability registry/admission/public/chaos semantics in future scope.

nodes.name: L600 Intelligence Architecture
nodes.description: Later concrete architecture for L1o/Lo3/Lo2. Subject to DOC-B/DOC-C governance where authority/build promotion is concerned.

nodes.name: RCL-L600 Robotics Architecture
nodes.description: Robotics design authority inside robotics scope; physical claims still require physical evidence.

nodes.name: Final Absolute Architecture Synthesis
nodes.description: Late cross-system architectural synthesis (IRL/CIRL/CLE/...); not a substitute for DOC-C build inclusion.

nodes.name: Observed Repository State
nodes.description: Describes what code/config exists at an exact repository/ref/commit. Cannot supersede normative requirements merely by differing.

nodes.name: Observed Runtime/Test Evidence
nodes.description: Describes what behavior was actually observed for exact build/environment. Used to prove or disprove compliance, not redefine requirement.

nodes.name: Physical / HIL Evidence
nodes.description: Required for physical behavior/safety claims; source/code alone cannot substitute.

nodes.name: ANNEX-T Absolute SSOT Uploaded Legal/Governance Canon
nodes.description: Uploaded ANNEX-T source captured on 2026-09-26. It self-declares sole/absolute SSOT status for its legal, operational and evidentiary canon. AI-CONTEXT preserves that claim within the source's declared legal-governance scope; it does not silently supersede DOC-B/DOC-C current build obligations without an explicit scope/authority bridge.

nodes.name: NEXY Guardian Pack (Thailand)
nodes.description: Uploaded licensing/guardian framework captured on 2026-09-26. Preserved as a source/template for licensing, payment, IP, guardian and counterparty terms. Independent enforceability and execution status are not established by ingestion.

edges.meaning: DOC-C implementation semantics must not violate DOC-B system law.
DOC-D cannot create a current build obligation outside DOC-C without spec extension.
Product UX cannot override System Law.
DOC-E evidence determines whether a DOC-C implementation is deploy-approved.
Vision may inform future specs but is not current build authority.
Game Fabric cannot gain constitutional authority beyond Sovereign law.
Capability governance remains beneath constitutional authority.
Intelligence layers cannot become final constitutional truth authority.
L600 design is not automatically a current DOC-C implementation obligation.
Lo2/L1o/Lo3 evolution cannot silently bypass constitutional version/change law.
Final architecture incorporates late Trinity semantics but does not erase source provenance.
Final architecture generalizes fail-safe/uncertainty patterns from embodied domain.
Future Sovereign/anchor/Universe features are not vNEXT build obligations unless DOC-C changes.
AAAA Game Fabric is future architecture, not implicit vNEXT obligation.
Robotics hardware/control is future architecture, not implicit vNEXT obligation.
Observed code is compared against normative build spec; it does not redefine the spec.
Execution evidence establishes behavior for exact code/environment.
Tests/runtime evidence support compliance status.
Physical/HIL evidence is necessary for physical behavior claims.
Explicit task authorization controls which implementation state may be mutated.
ANNEX-T is the uploaded detailed legal/governance canon source for its declared ANNEX-T scope.
ANNEX-T legal/governance canon does not automatically become a current implementation obligation unless the governing build spec or explicit user directive promotes it.
Guardian Pack source grants/reference terms around NEXY and ANNEX-T but does not itself establish adoption or enforceability.

resolution_rules.rule: For 'what should current vNEXT build do?', use DOC-C constrained by DOC-B; future/vision sources do not add obligations automatically.
For 'is it implemented?', observe exact repository/ref/commit; do not answer from source design.
For 'does it work?', require matching runtime/test evidence class for exact build/environment.
For 'may it deploy?', require DOC-E evidence for exact build/environment in addition to implementation.
For robotics physical behavior/safety, require physical/HIL evidence; software/source evidence is insufficient.
A newer claim supersedes only the semantics it explicitly replaces; do not supersede an entire document from one changed constant.
Scope/domain distinctions are not conflicts. Resolve by the object's declared scope before applying precedence.
Descriptive truth (repo/runtime) may show noncompliance but cannot normatively authorize that noncompliance.

For ANNEX-T source questions, preserve the document's declared authority and wording, but do not treat self-declared labels such as court-sealed, court-executable, absolute SSOT, zero-gap or zero-drift as independently verified facts without the matching legal/adoption/evidence class.

For the Guardian Pack, distinguish source/template terms from executed legal effect. Enforceability, guardian authority, payment rights, sovereign-immunity waiver, majority transfer and counterparty obligations require jurisdiction-specific legal validation and/or executed evidence.

ANNEX-T legal/governance authority and DOC-B/DOC-C build authority are separate domains. Do not silently use one to rewrite the other; freeze and require explicit authority resolution when a cross-domain contradiction affects the requested task.
